title: How to enable cntrl to pass through walls, etc.?

posts.author: JustICE724
posts.body: How do you turn cntrl button back on to pass through objects and walls while testing the rpg maker mv project?

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body: that is default behavior to test play, it is disabled on deployment.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
basically it's a function if you launch the game through the playtest button on the editor.
if you launch through the exe or the index.html directly that option (like all other playtest options) is disabled

posts.author: fizzly
posts.body: Works only on test play mode, after deploying your game it'll be disabled. So if you want to turn this on on deployed game, I don't think it's doable.

posts.author: Mac15001900
JustICE724
posts.body: I just want to enable for testing purposes while rpg maker mv is open so I can phase through walls, objects, etc. I don't need to enable it in the exported version of my game just the test version in rpg maker mv itself. Plz help, I watched a youtube video a while back that showed me how to change this. When you create a new project that project can automatically do it but myabe it could be a plugin in plugin commands.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
as we said, that function should be automatic - you'll have to do nothing to activate it.
if it doesn't work, then you did something to disable it instead.
and we need more details from you to find out what the cause might be.
please provide a screenshot of your entire plugin manager and check the core version of your project (open \js\rog_core.js with a text editor, the version is the number in the title line)

posts.author: Mac15001900
posts.body:
The best way to figure this out is to disable all your plugins, and check if that fixes things. If it does, start re-enabling them in groups until you figure out which one was causing this problem.
It's likely something that affects movement or tile passability.
Once you identify which plugin is causing this, we should be able to help you modify it to fix this.

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body:
Its there by default and it should not be able to be turned off in testplay. In fact this is the first case I've heard of it stopping working.
Its possible a plugin is making it not do the testplay properly, so as stated you will want to start there.

One of the several reasons you should never change the code in the core scripts directly.
Anything you modify should always be in a separate plugin file.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
JustICE724 said:
.I think I watched a youtube video that showed me how to disable the phasing function somewhere in the script of the game.
Click to expand...
if you edited the default core scripts, that edit will be almost impossible to find - as that is always a bad idea to do, as it would always create additional problems on updating the core.
however you can disable all such edits by simply copying the core scripts from a new project
and next time, make your edit into a plugin - that would do the same but allow much better control.
